items.passage:
Brine and coal smoke fill the narrow compartment,
and the whistle shrieks twice over the South Side roofs.
Birdie holds the paper parcel Mattie pressed on him,
the last perch, wrapped the way it always was,
string knotted twice against the jolting road ahead.
For eleven summers the old man's cart
had stopped at Birdie's stoop each Friday, never late.
Now the boy is the one departing, northbound for good,
and he finds the parcel's weight ______:
not heavy, yet steady in his lap,
as faithful as the cart had been,
as if Mattie's Fridays had climbed aboard with him.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: burdensome
reassuring
indifferent
fragile
items.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에서 꾸러미의 무게는 무겁지 않지만 무릎 위에서 '한결같고' 수레처럼 '충실하다'고 묘사된다. 또 앞부분에서 Mattie의 수레가 11년 동안 한 번도 늦지 않았다는 점이 제시되어, 꾸러미가 떠나는 소년에게 위안이 되는 존재임을 알 수 있다. 따라서 B가 가장 적절하다. A는 '무겁지 않다'는 표현과 충돌하고, C와 D는 '충실하다', '한결같다'는 단서와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Years later, I still remember how Nikos and I fought over the noodle stall's chili flakes instead of the thing that mattered. He had been my literature teacher, and I had abandoned the scholarship he arranged for me. At the stall near Karakoy, he insisted the vendor used too much pepper; I insisted the pepper was the point. Neither of us mentioned the letter of recommendation he had written and I had never used. Our argument about the noodles was, I now see, ______: small enough to survive, it carried the larger quarrel neither of us could say aloud. "Zeynep," he finally said, using my full name the way he had in class, "eat before it gets cold." I did, and we spoke of the weather.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: a distraction
a resolution
a substitute
a coincidence
items.explanation: 첫 문장에서 화자는 두 사람이 '중요한 일 대신' 고춧가루로 다퉜다고 말한다. 빈칸 뒤에서도 그 다툼이 말로 꺼내지 못한 더 큰 갈등을 '실어 날랐다'고 설명하므로, 국수 논쟁은 진짜 갈등을 대신하는 것이다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 그럴듯하지만 다툼이 큰 갈등을 담아냈다는 점을 놓치고, B와 D는 갈등이 해결되지 않았고 우연이 아니라는 맥락과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: "Go," my mother said, before I had even mentioned the letter. Snow had sealed the cabin door outside Hamburg for two days, and I had spent them heating soup and counting her pills. The scholarship from the conservatory meant leaving her for a year; my brother Thiago had already written that he could not come home to help. I told her I would decline. She waved the idea away, but her hand trembled, and I could hear how much the offer of her blessing cost her. Her encouragement was ______: generous in its words, yet shadowed by a fear she would not name. That night I read the letter again by the stove and left it unanswered on the table.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: insincere
careless
mocking
conflicted
items.explanation: 어머니는 떠나라고 말하지만 손이 떨리고, 화자는 그 축복이 어머니에게 큰 대가였음을 느낀다. 빈칸 뒤에서도 격려가 말로는 너그럽지만 말하지 않은 두려움에 가려져 있다고 설명된다. 두 단서를 연결하면 어머니의 격려는 상반된 감정이 섞인 것이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 어머니의 말이 거짓이라는 근거가 없고, B와 C는 진지하고 떨리는 태도와 어긋난다.

items.passage: Who would have guessed the press room would smell of cardamom? Rukhsana, sixteen, had cooked the rice and dhal for the whole night crew in Colombo while her aunt supervised from the doorway, arms folded. When the foreman, Cormac, raised his tin plate and praised the aunt's cooking, Rukhsana laughed along, clattering the pots, eager to keep the evening light. Then her aunt said nothing to correct him. Rukhsana's laughter thinned. She stacked the plates more slowly, noticing how the ink-stained hands of the printers kept reaching for food she alone had measured and stirred. Later, scrubbing the pot, she said only, "The tamarind was mine." Her aunt looked at her for a long moment, then nodded once toward Cormac, as if to say, tell him yourself.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From lighthearted cheer to quiet resentment as Rukhsana sees her work credited to another.
From open anger to reluctant acceptance as Rukhsana forgives her aunt's silence.
From nervous anticipation to relief as the printers finally praise Rukhsana's cooking.
From playful teasing to formal politeness as Rukhsana addresses the foreman directly.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Rukhsana는 냄비를 달그락거리며 웃고 분위기를 가볍게 유지하려 한다. 그러나 이모가 Cormac의 착각을 바로잡지 않자 웃음이 잦아들고, 자신이 혼자 만든 음식에 손을 뻗는 인쇄공들을 바라보며 '타마린드는 내 거였어요'라고 말한다. 따라서 어조는 밝은 유쾌함에서 조용한 억울함으로 바뀌므로 A가 정답이다. B는 처음부터 분노가 드러나지 않고, C와 D는 칭찬이 다른 사람에게 갔다는 핵심과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: "Careful, that bow is older than both of us," Gunnar said, grinning, as Callum fumbled it beside the cafe's sugar bowl. Trains hissed beyond the Rotterdam windows, and the conductor teased the boy about his cold coffee and his crooked collar. Callum asked whose bow it had been. Gunnar's grin faded. He turned the bow slowly in his hands, thumb resting on the worn grip where another thumb had worn it first. He said that his teacher had played with it for forty years and had left it to him without a note. For a while he only watched the departures board. Then he set the bow in front of Callum and pushed it gently across the table.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From irritation to amusement as Gunnar forgives Callum's clumsiness at the table.
From playful banter to solemn reflection as Gunnar recalls the bow's former owner.
From anxious hurry to calm patience as Gunnar waits for a delayed train to arrive.
From formal instruction to open grief as Gunnar refuses to discuss his teacher.
items.explanation: 처음에 Gunnar는 웃으며 Callum의 식은 커피와 삐뚤어진 옷깃을 놀린다. Callum이 활의 주인을 묻자 미소가 사라지고, 그는 스승이 남긴 활의 닳은 손잡이를 만지며 말없이 출발 안내판을 바라본다. 따라서 장난스러운 대화에서 엄숙한 회상으로 바뀌므로 B가 정답이다. A는 처음 어조를 짜증으로 잘못 보고, D는 Gunnar가 스승 이야기를 실제로 들려준다는 점과 어긋나며, C는 기차 지연과 무관하다.

items.passage: When I was nineteen, my stepfather and I worked the dark hours at Rivka's bakery in Haifa, shaping dough before the shutters rose. He had paid my first year of tuition with money meant for his own retirement, and neither of us ever spoke of it. For months I treated those mornings as a chore, sulking over the cold flour and his habit of humming off-key. Then one morning Rivka mentioned, offhand, that he had taken extra shifts all winter. I watched him fold the challah with his cracked knuckles and felt my impatience drain into something closer to awe. I began arriving early to light the ovens before he came. He never asked why, and I never explained.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From gratitude to disappointment as the narrator learns her stepfather resented the cost.
From cheerful curiosity to suspicion as the narrator questions Rivka's real motives.
From grudging irritation to humbled admiration as the narrator grasps his sacrifice.
From nostalgic warmth to sharp regret as the narrator recalls leaving the bakery.
items.explanation: 앞부분의 화자는 새벽 일을 귀찮은 일로 여기며 차가운 밀가루와 의붓아버지의 음치 허밍에 투덜댄다. Rivka가 그가 겨울 내내 추가 근무를 했다고 알려 준 뒤, 화자는 갈라진 손마디를 보며 짜증이 경외에 가까운 감정으로 바뀌었다고 말한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 의붓아버지가 원망했다는 근거가 없고, B와 D는 Rivka에 대한 의심이나 빵집을 떠난 후회가 지문에 없다.

items.passage: Two cups of cold tea sat between Meera and me on the reading-room table in Accra, where we had met every Thursday for three years to work on her novel. When the translation won the prize, I expected those Thursdays to feel like a celebration. For the first week they did; we laughed at the reviewers who praised my "invisible" English, and Meera read the congratulations aloud in a theatrical voice. But the publishers soon wanted a second book in half the time, and interviewers asked which of us had really written the famous closing chapter. Meera began correcting my drafts in ink instead of pencil. I began to dread the creak of the library door. We still met on Thursdays, though we spoke mostly about deadlines.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From weary routine to renewed excitement as the prize revives the partnership.
From resentment to forgiveness as Meera accepts the narrator's version of the chapter.
From quiet focus to open rivalry as Meera refuses to share credit in public.
From buoyant celebration to strained unease as success brings new pressures.
items.explanation: 수상 직후 첫 주에는 두 사람이 서평을 두고 웃고 Meera가 축하 인사를 과장된 목소리로 읽는 등 들뜬 분위기다. 그러나 출판사의 촉박한 요구와 누가 마지막 장을 썼느냐는 질문이 이어지자 Meera는 잉크로 고치기 시작하고 화자는 도서관 문소리를 두려워하게 된다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. C는 그럴듯하지만 공개적인 경쟁이나 공로 거부는 나오지 않으며, A와 B는 변화 방향이 반대이거나 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Diesel and wet asphalt hung over the Taipei bus depot when Yuying finally brought Larissa down from the mountain trail. The hiker had been missing since dawn; the ranger had found her near a washed-out bridge and walked her six kilometers back. At the depot, other rangers crowded around, clapping Yuying on the shoulder. She shrugged them off, saying anyone could have followed the footprints. Yet when Larissa thanked her, Yuying recited, unprompted, the exact turns she had taken, the bridge she had judged unsafe, and the shortcut she had refused. Later, alone by the ticket window, she smoothed the creases from her uniform twice and checked her reflection in the glass before boarding the last bus home.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a rescue, presents a character's dismissal of praise, and then reveals details hinting at her hidden pride.
It introduces a hiker's mistake, explains its causes, and then describes how the hiker avoids repeating it later.
It recounts a celebration at the depot, then shifts to a flashback explaining why the ranger joined the service.
It presents an argument between two rangers and then shows how the hiker eventually settles their disagreement.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 Yuying이 Larissa를 구조해 온 과정을 서술한다. 이어 동료들의 칭찬을 누구라도 할 수 있었다며 털어내는 모습을 보여 준 뒤, 묻지도 않은 경로를 자세히 늘어놓고 혼자 제복을 다듬는 행동으로 숨은 자부심을 드러낸다. 따라서 A가 전개 순서와 초점 이동을 정확히 설명한다. B, C, D는 지문에 없는 원인 분석, 회상, 논쟁을 구조로 제시한다.

items.passage: We boarded the night bus in Krakow just after midnight, Rafaela and I, the way we used to after shows when we were the two halves of a cabaret act. Back then she sang and I played piano, and the audience never guessed how often we argued backstage. Now she leaned against the fogged window and explained her plan: we would tell Dainius, the festival director, that our old act had never really broken up, that we had simply been touring abroad. If he believed us, he would give us the closing slot. I said nothing for several stops. I was thinking of the letter I had sent him two years earlier, announcing our split in my own careful handwriting.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a performance, recounts the audience's reaction, and then explains why the act ended.
It recalls the women's past partnership, lays out a deceptive plan, and then reveals a fact that threatens it.
It introduces a festival director, describes his doubts, and then shows the women persuading him.
It presents a quarrel on the bus, traces its origin backstage, and then depicts the women reconciling.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 두 사람이 카바레 공연 파트너였던 과거를 떠올린다. 이어 Rafaela가 Dainius에게 팀이 해체되지 않았다고 거짓말하자는 계획을 설명하고, 마지막에 화자가 이미 해체를 알리는 편지를 보냈다는 사실이 드러나 계획이 위태로워진다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 공연 장면이 중심이 아니고, C와 D는 감독 설득이나 화해 장면이 지문에 없다.

items.passage: By the third week of our evening Latvian class in Riga, I had noticed that Bronislaw, my neighbor and a retired sailor, always knew the answers. He had sailed these waters for forty years and picked up the language on the docks. So when our teacher held a vocabulary contest, I assumed he would win easily. Instead he stumbled on the word for "harbor," of all things, and I took the small prize, a chocolate bar. At first I was simply pleased. Weeks later, though, I heard him chatting fluently with the janitor about tides and ropes, and I understood that he had stumbled deliberately. Now, whenever I unwrap chocolate, I picture his weathered hands folding the empty contest sheet.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a contest, praises the teacher's methods, and then recommends a way of learning a language.
It introduces a sailor's past, recounts his voyages, and then explains why he decided to settle in Riga.
It presents an assumption, recounts an outcome that defies it, and then reveals the reason for that outcome.
It recounts a rivalry, describes an argument it causes, and then shows how the two neighbors reconcile.
items.explanation: 화자는 먼저 Bronislaw가 늘 답을 알기 때문에 대회에서 쉽게 이길 것이라고 예상한다. 그러나 그는 '항구'라는 쉬운 단어에서 틀리고 화자가 상을 받으며, 몇 주 뒤 그가 유창하게 말하는 것을 듣고서야 일부러 졌다는 이유가 드러난다. 따라서 예상, 예상을 뒤집는 결과, 그 이유의 순서를 말한 C가 정답이다. A, B, D는 교수법 추천, 항해 이야기, 말다툼과 화해처럼 지문의 전개와 다른 구조를 제시한다.

items.passage: I came to Valparaiso to survey the old metro platform, a job I expected to finish in a single afternoon. Itzel, the platform keeper, met me with a ring of keys and a thermos of coffee, polite but guarded. As I measured the cracked tiles, she mentioned a girl from the neighborhood who waited here every morning to watch the first train. Itzel had promised her the platform would never close. My report, I knew, would almost certainly recommend closing it. For an hour I worked in silence, the tape measure clicking. Then I asked Itzel to show me where the girl stood, and I photographed that spot first, before anything else.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a girl's routine, explains the metro's history, and then predicts the platform's closure.
It recounts a dispute between two officials, then shows how a child resolves their conflict.
It introduces a guarded keeper, describes their friendship, and then celebrates the platform's renovation.
It presents a routine task, introduces a promise that complicates it, and then shows the narrator's response.
items.explanation: 화자는 오후 한나절이면 끝날 일상적인 측량 업무로 글을 시작한다. 이어 Itzel이 소녀에게 승강장이 닫히지 않을 것이라 약속했다는 사실이 나오고, 화자의 보고서가 폐쇄를 권고할 것이라는 점과 충돌한다. 마지막에 화자는 소녀가 서던 자리를 먼저 촬영하며 그 긴장에 반응하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 역사 설명이 없고, B와 C는 관리 간 분쟁이나 개보수 축하가 지문에 없다.

items.passage: Once the rains had ruined the spring firing, half the pots at the Lima studio had cracked in the kiln, and Cleotilde blamed the new teacher. Eulalio had arrived only that season, and she was sure his unfamiliar glazes had caused the damage. For weeks she worked at the far end of the bench, answering him in single words. __One afternoon he set a cracked bowl in front of her and asked her to find exactly where the clay had given way.__ She traced the fracture with her thumb and found a pocket of trapped air, a flaw in her own wedging, not his glaze. She said nothing, but the next morning she moved her stool to the middle of the bench.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It marks a turning point by prompting Cleotilde to discover the true cause of the failure.
It shows Eulalio defending himself by openly blaming Cleotilde for the cracked pots.
It explains why the spring rains made the kiln firing unusually difficult that season.
It introduces a conflict between Eulalio and the studio's owner over the damaged work.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Cleotilde는 실패를 새 선생님의 유약 탓으로 돌리며 거리를 둔다. 밑줄 문장에서 Eulalio가 갈라진 그릇을 건네 금이 간 곳을 찾게 하자, 그녀는 결함이 자신의 반죽에 있었음을 발견하고 다음 날 자리를 옮긴다. 따라서 밑줄 문장은 진짜 원인을 깨닫게 하는 전환점이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 그가 직접 비난하지 않으므로 틀리고, C와 D는 밑줄 문장의 내용과 무관하다.

items.passage: Siti had not come to forgive anyone. She had come to the school music room in Thessaloniki only because Kostas, her father's old bandmate, had asked to return something. He stood by the dusty upright piano, turning his hat in his hands, while she kept her coat buttoned. __He set a cassette on the lid: her father's voice, singing a lullaby with her name in it.__ She had believed her father left without a thought of her. Kostas explained that the tape had been recorded the week before he went, and that he had been too ashamed to send it. Siti did not press play. But she unbuttoned her coat, sat on the piano bench, and asked Kostas to tell her about the band.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reveals that Kostas, not Siti's father, was responsible for the family's separation.
It introduces evidence that challenges Siti's belief that her father had forgotten her.
It describes the music room's equipment in order to establish the story's setting.
It shows Kostas mocking Siti's reluctance to remember her father and his music.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장 바로 뒤에서 Siti는 아버지가 자신을 생각하지도 않고 떠났다고 믿어 왔다고 나온다. 밑줄 문장의 카세트에는 그녀의 이름이 들어간 자장가가 담겨 있어 그 믿음을 흔들고, 이후 그녀는 코트를 풀고 밴드 이야기를 청한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 Kostas가 가족 분리의 책임자라는 근거가 없고, C는 배경 묘사로만 보았으며, D의 조롱은 지문에 없다.

items.passage: Years later, I can still smell the steam and chalk of Folasade's back room in Lyon, where I took my son to have his first suit hemmed before he left for college. While the tailor pinned his cuffs, he wandered to a corkboard crowded with faded photographs. Among them he found one of me at nineteen, Elodie in a borrowed coat, standing in that same room on the morning I left home. He laughed at my enormous collar. __I did not tell him that I had cried in the train toilet all the way to Paris.__ Instead I said the coat had been warm. He studied the picture a little longer, then asked Folasade if he could take a copy with him.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why the narrator chose Folasade's shop for her son's first suit.
It suggests the narrator regrets ever leaving Lyon to study in Paris.
It reveals a private memory the narrator withholds as her son prepares to leave.
It contrasts the narrator's fashion sense with her son's as he mocks the coat.
items.explanation: 아들이 사진 속 큰 옷깃을 보고 웃자, 밑줄 문장에서 화자는 자신이 집을 떠나며 파리까지 울었던 기억을 말하지 않았다고 밝힌다. 이어 그녀는 코트가 따뜻했다고만 말하는데, 이는 떠나는 아들 앞에서 아픈 기억을 감춘 것이다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. B는 그럴듯하지만 떠난 것 자체를 후회한다는 근거가 없고, A와 D는 밑줄 문장의 역할과 관계가 없다.

items.passage: On my first visit back to Manchester after the move, Josiah took me to the bookbinder's workshop where we had apprenticed together as teenagers. He showed me the guest book we had bound for the owner's anniversary, still displayed on the front shelf. Everyone praised it, he said, every visitor for six years. I turned the pages and saw it at once: signature four was sewn upside down, a mistake I had made and hidden by trimming the edges. __Josiah ran his palm over the cover with obvious pride.__ I opened my mouth to confess, then closed it again. Outside, the rain started, and we stood under the awning eating chips from a paper cone.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that Josiah has secretly known about the narrator's error all along.
It reveals that the workshop's owner has refused to display the guest book.
It suggests that Josiah is jealous of the praise the narrator received for the book.
It heightens the narrator's dilemma by showing how much the book means to Josiah.
items.explanation: 앞 문장에서 화자는 자신만 아는 제본 실수를 발견하고, 밑줄 문장에서 Josiah는 자랑스럽게 표지를 쓰다듬는다. 바로 뒤에서 화자가 고백하려다 입을 다무는 것으로 보아, 밑줄 문장은 친구의 자부심을 보여 주어 고백의 딜레마를 키운다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 Josiah가 실수를 알았다는 근거가 없고, B와 C는 책이 진열되어 있다는 점과 질투의 부재에 어긋난다.

items.passage: Three things I knew about Lorenzo before that night: he sold the best sfogliatelle in Naples, he never shared recipes, and he never seemed tired. At two in the morning I went to the all-night pharmacy for burn ointment and found him at the counter, buying the same thing. His forearms were striped with old scars from oven racks. The pharmacist greeted him by name and asked whether he had slept at all this week. Lorenzo laughed and said sleep was for bakers with smaller ovens. I had always believed his reputation came from some secret ingredient. Walking home, I passed his shop, lit and humming, the windows fogged, and I slowed my steps until I was well past it.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Lorenzo?
options: Dismissive scorn for a rival she believes has cheated his way to success.
Lingering envy that grows stronger once she learns his secret recipe.
Detached indifference toward a baker whose work she rarely notices.
Grudging respect for a rival whose success she now sees was hard earned.
items.explanation: 화자는 Lorenzo의 명성이 비밀 재료 덕분이라고 믿어 왔지만, 약국에서 그의 오븐 화상 흉터와 잠을 못 잔 생활을 알게 된다. 귀갓길에 그의 가게 앞에서 걸음을 늦추는 행동은 경쟁자에 대한 마지못한 존중을 보여 준다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. B는 경쟁심을 반영해 그럴듯하지만 비밀 레시피를 알게 된 것이 아니고, A와 C는 노력의 발견과 관심 어린 시선에 어긋난다.

items.passage: Two tiffin boxes rested on the parapet of the stone bridge, one for Mohan and one for me, as they had every evening for thirty years. Below us the creek carried the smell of salt and diesel toward the sea. Mohan rarely spoke on these evenings, and I had long stopped expecting him to. That night he said only that the company in Pune had offered him the post. One of us had to stay with our mothers in Mumbai; we both knew it. I wanted to tell him that he deserved the post more than I ever would, that his quiet had always been a kind of steadiness I leaned on. Instead I slid his tiffin closer and said the dal was getting cold.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Mohan?
options: Deep but unspoken affection for a friend whose departure he is prepared to accept.
Open resentment of a friend who is abandoning their shared duty to their mothers.
Amused impatience with a friend whose long silences have always irritated him.
Cautious suspicion of a friend he believes is hiding the real reason for leaving.
items.explanation: 화자는 Mohan의 침묵을 오래 받아들여 왔고, 그 고요함이 자신이 기대던 '한결같음'이었다고 생각한다. 또 Mohan이 그 자리를 더 받을 자격이 있다고 말하고 싶어 하면서도 실제로는 도시락을 밀어 주며 달이 식는다고만 말한다. 이는 말로 표현하지 않는 깊은 애정과 그의 떠남을 받아들이는 태도이므로 A가 정답이다. B, C, D의 원망, 짜증, 의심은 지문의 근거와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: When Lachlan finally carried the tin box up the lighthouse stairs in Galway, I had not spoken to him in four years, and our mother had been gone for two. The letters inside were hers, written to us during the winters she kept the light alone. I expected complaints; she had been a sharp, impatient woman, and I had left home partly to escape her. Instead the letters described the gannets diving at dawn, the exact color of the sea before a storm, and how she saved the best biscuits for when we visited. Reading them aloud, Lachlan's voice cracked. I found myself revising her as I listened, softening the hard edges I had carried. Outside, the lamp began its slow turn over the water.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward her mother?
options: Lasting bitterness that the letters ultimately confirm rather than ease.
Growing tenderness as the letters complicate her earlier resentment.
Polite curiosity about a woman she barely knew as a young child.
Quiet guilt over having neglected her mother during her final years.
items.explanation: 화자는 어머니를 날카롭고 성급한 사람으로 기억해 불평이 담긴 편지를 예상했다. 그러나 편지에는 새벽의 가넷, 폭풍 전 바다 빛깔, 자식들을 위해 아껴 둔 비스킷이 담겨 있었고, 화자는 듣는 동안 어머니에 대한 기억을 부드럽게 고쳐 간다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 처음 태도에만 머물고, C와 D는 어머니를 잘 알지 못했다거나 죄책감을 느낀다는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Kommetjie's post office was a single room with a sagging counter, and Nandi had come there every Tuesday for a year to interpret for Mandla. He was writing a history of his village in isiXhosa, letter by letter, to a university archive that answered only in English. Early on, Nandi translated his sentences almost word for word, and the archivist's replies grew polite and brief. Over the months she began asking Mandla what each memory meant to him before choosing her English, and the replies lengthened into questions. Now the history stood unfinished at chapter nine, and Mandla asked whether she would carry on alone if he could not. Outside, a delivery van idled in the dust, its driver sorting parcels on the warm bonnet.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Nandi and Mandla meet weekly at a post office to send letters about his village to an archive.
Mandla's history records village life that the university archive values above all others.
Nandi's growing attention to Mandla's meaning has made her a true partner in his work.
Translating between languages is always difficult, even for experienced interpreters.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Nandi는 문장을 거의 직역했고 기록 보관소의 답장은 짧았다. 뒷부분에서 그녀가 각 기억의 의미를 먼저 묻고 번역하자 답장이 질문으로 길어졌고, 결국 Mandla는 미완성 작업을 혼자서라도 이어 달라고 부탁한다. 두 대비를 연결하면 Nandi가 단순 통역자를 넘어 작업의 동반자가 되었다는 C가 요지다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 소재는 같지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: After the irrigation pump exploded, Lars and Noor stood in the abandoned orchard outside Marrakesh, deciding what to tell his father. Lars, the landlord's son, suggested they say the pump had simply worn out with age. Noor, whose family rented the farmhouse, pointed out that he had run it dry all afternoon to fill a swimming trough. He argued that the truth would only get her father blamed for poor upkeep. By evening, they had written three versions of the story, each a little more careful than the last, and Noor insisted they keep the one that named Lars. He read it twice, then signed it. Overhead, the bare apricot branches clicked together in the wind like loose shutters.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how an irrigation pump was destroyed in an orchard outside Marrakesh.
To describe the orchard's decline after the landlord's family abandoned it.
To suggest that every accident has more than one equally valid explanation.
To show how Noor's insistence moves Lars from evasion toward responsibility.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Lars는 펌프가 낡아서 고장 났다고 둘러대자고 제안하지만 Noor는 그가 펌프를 공회전시킨 사실을 지적한다. 뒷부분에서 Noor가 Lars의 이름이 들어간 버전을 고집하고 Lars는 그것을 두 번 읽고 서명한다. 두 지점을 연결하면 지문은 Noor의 고집이 Lars를 회피에서 책임으로 이끄는 과정을 보여 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 사고 일화만 요약했고, B는 소재는 같지만 목적이 다르며, C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.
